scope.stylesheet: src/app/globals.css (Drum Roll block, direction seed ffed24ea)
scope.note: Committed light. The route sits in DARK_EXCEPTIONS in src/components/layout/site-shell.tsx so it never inherits Broadcast Dark's .bx-dark ground.

dr-ink-dim.note: Tinted from the ground's own warmth, never a flat gray. ~7:1 on the ground.

result.purpose: The drawn name, in brand orange, under the wheel. Nothing else uses this step.

headline.purpose: The prize line above the wheel; its lede words drop to 400 in Dim Ink inside the same line.

title.purpose: The page's own name in the header row. A label, not a hero.

section.purpose: Shelf headings (Who is in?, Prizes). One step above body, never a display step.

body.purpose: All prose and reported lines in Dim Ink; bold figures return to Ink with tabular numerals.

wedge.purpose: 8.4px inside a 208-unit viewBox, set at the rim running inward, half-turned past six o'clock.

readout.purpose: Geist Mono, tabular: the committed seed and ticket counts only. Never a costume for labels.

shadows.name: wheel-drop
shadows.purpose: The whole wheel face resting on the ground as one object.

shadows.name: hub
shadows.purpose: The machined hub boss over its radial graphite gradient.

shadows.name: flapper
shadows.purpose: The sprung pointer reading as above the wheel it rides.

shadows.name: landing
shadows.purpose: Warm shadow on the winning wedge only, which is also drawn 3 units proud of the rim.

shadows.name: key-rest
shadows.purpose: The moulded spin key at rest: inner bottom bevel plus short contact shadow.

shadows.name: key-hover
shadows.purpose: Contact shadow deepening under the pointer.

shadows.name: key-press
shadows.purpose: Struck key: translate 2px down and collapse to a single inset line.

shadows.name: quiet-ring
shadows.purpose: The inset ring that stands in for a border on quiet keys.

motion.name: spin
motion.value: 4600ms, 5 turns + distance to target, eased 1 - (1 - t)^4
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: quick to speed, then a long honest tail where a wedge boundary can still change the answer. Driven by direct style writes, so React never renders a frame.

motion.name: land
motion.purpose: The winning wedge coming up proud and staying there.

motion.name: flapper-ride
motion.value: up to 17deg, engaged within 7deg of a peg
motion.purpose: Each peg pushes the flapper and drops it the instant it passes, so deflection rides up and snaps rather than oscillating.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: A control that feels struck rather than faded.

motion.name: wedge-fill
motion.purpose: A wedge taking or losing the accent fill.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions 1ms; spin resolves straight to the landed state; landing holds scale(1.022) with no animation
motion.purpose: Reduced motion gets the answer, not a shortened show.

breakpoints.name: row-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Below this, rows stack and left-align and section heads pack left, keeping controls out of the site's fixed mobile menu gutter.

components.name: Spin Key
components.description: The only filled control in the world: solid brand orange, moulded by an inner bottom bevel, struck rather than faded on press.
components.css: .ds-key{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:.5rem;min-height:3.25rem;padding:.8rem 2.4rem;border:0;border-radius:3px;background:#f26522;color:#fff;font-family:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:1.0625rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.02em;cursor:pointer;box-shadow:inset 0 -2px 3px oklch(0.44 0.15 40/.55),0 2px 4px oklch(0.24 0.02 70/.24);transition:translate 90ms ease-out,box-shadow 90ms ease-out}.ds-key:hover{box-shadow:inset 0 -2px 3px oklch(0.44 0.15 40/.55),0 4px 9px oklch(0.24 0.02 70/.3)}.ds-key:active{translate:0 2px;box-shadow:inset 0 -1px 0 oklch(0.48 0.16 40)}.ds-key:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #f26522;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px}

components.name: The Wheel
components.description: The signature device: wedge widths are ticket counts, three cycling warm tones, labels at the rim running inward, pegs, rim, bevel and hub, with the pointer flapper on top. Shown here landed.
components.css: .ds-wheel{position:relative;width:min(80vw,18rem);aspect-ratio:1;margin-inline:auto;display:grid;place-items:center}.ds-wheel-face{width:100%;height:100%;overflow:visible;filter:drop-shadow(0 16px 26px oklch(0.24 0.02 70/.26))}.ds-wedge{stroke:oklch(0.26 0.01 70);stroke-width:.6;transition:fill 260ms ease-out}.ds-t0{fill:oklch(0.988 0.004 92)}.ds-t1{fill:oklch(0.928 0.019 84)}.ds-t2{fill:oklch(0.858 0.029 76)}.ds-wedge-won{fill:#f26522;filter:drop-shadow(0 3px 7px oklch(0.42 0.14 40/.45))}.ds-wedge-name{fill:oklch(0.22 0.008 70);font-family:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:8.4px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.01em}.ds-wedge-name-won{fill:#fff;font-weight:700}.ds-peg{stroke:oklch(0.63 0.012 75);stroke-width:2.6;stroke-linecap:round}.ds-rim{fill:none;stroke:oklch(0.26 0.01 70);stroke-width:11}.ds-bevel{fill:none;stroke:oklch(0.52 0.012 70);stroke-width:1.6}.ds-hub{position:absolute;width:13%;aspect-ratio:1;border-radius:50%;background:radial-gradient(circle at 38% 32%,oklch(0.46 0.01 70),oklch(0.24 0.01 70) 62%);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px oklch(0.6 0.01 70/.5),0 2px 5px oklch(0.2 0.01 70/.5)}.ds-pointer{position:absolute;top:-.35rem;left:50%;translate:-50% 0;z-index:2;filter:drop-shadow(0 2px 3px oklch(0.24 0.02 70/.4))}

narrative.overview:
The wheel, built like equipment instead of a widget. A quiet warm hall white carries one heavy object with real geometry: a machined hub, a turned rim with a bevelled inner edge, pegs standing proud of the band, and a sprung flapper that each peg pushes up and drops as it passes. Everything else on the page — roster, prizes, seed, controls — is flat type on the ground, separated by hairlines, with no cards anywhere.

The wheel earns its place on one argument, and the argument is visual: wedge widths are ticket counts, so five tickets is a wedge five times wider and the odds are the picture rather than a number somebody has to be told. The world refuses two predictable alternatives — the flat conic-gradient wheel with a result modal, and the SaaS tool page that buries the odds behind a ticket count — and it refuses the rainbow wheel specifically, because a colour per name is why everybody else's labels are unreadable. The governing constraint is legibility: one name read fast off a phone held up in a room.

Depth here is contact, not float. Shadows are short and dark-warm, sitting a part against the ground; the wheel's own drop shadow and the winning wedge's proud scale are the only places the surface lifts at all. Motion is one authored moment — the spin — and nothing else animates for decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Warm hall-white ground, ink and hairlines, no cards and no panels
Wedges cycle three warm neutrals, never a colour per name
Brand orange spends itself on exactly two things: the pointer and the wedge that wins
Wedge angle equals ticket share; the odds are drawn, never stated
Schibsted Grotesk carries every word a person reads; Geist Mono only where the surface reports data back
3px corners on every control — machined, not rounded
One spin: 4.6s, five turns, exponential ease-out, resolved instantly under reduced motion

rules.name: The One Saturated Event Rule
rules.body: Brand orange belongs to the pointer and the landed wedge. A saturated colour anywhere else — a chip, a heading, a filled secondary button — competes with the only moment the page exists for.

rules.name: The No Colour Per Name Rule
rules.body: Wedges cycle exactly three warm neutrals by index. Naming-by-hue is the failure mode of every draw wheel on the internet: it destroys the label contrast that the whole surface is built to protect.

rules.name: The Two Ink Steps Rule
rules.body: Ink and Dim Ink. There is no third, fainter tone; if something needs to recede further it is not on this page.

rules.name: The Brand Orange Is Fixed Rule
rules.body: #f26522 is never darkened or retinted to improve a contrast ratio — a standing brand commitment in PRODUCT.md. Here it is moot for reading anyway: orange never carries body text. It is a wedge fill under 700-weight white, a solid key fill, and a 2px focus ring.

rules.name: The Mono Reports Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only where the surface is reporting a value back that someone will read aloud and check afterwards — the seed, ticket counts, the manual-paste field. It is never a costume for a label or a heading.

rules.name: The Every Ticket Is Labelled Rule
rules.body: A wedge degrades its label rather than dropping it: full name, then first name plus surname initial, then first name truncated, then two initials, and only under 3.2° does it go blank. A bucket where somebody's ticket is unlabelled is a bucket the room cannot audit.

rules.name: The Wheel Owns The Fold Rule
rules.body: The wheel, the drawing line, the seed readout and the spin key fit one viewport together. Anything that would push the key below the fold gets a smaller wheel, not a scroll.

rules.name: The Contact-Not-Float Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this world is short, warm-dark and tied to an object that is physically resting on or above the ground. There is no ambient glow, no coloured halo, and no elevation used to signal hierarchy.

rules.name: The Wheel Decides Nothing Rule
rules.body: The winner is chosen against a seed the room has already seen and logged before the wheel is told anything; the spin is presentation of a result that already exists. No randomness lives in the wheel.

dos: Do size wedges by ticket share and let the widths carry the odds. If a number has to be stated to explain the chances, the drawing has failed.
Do keep brand orange to the flapper, the landed wedge, the focus ring and the caret.
Do separate blocks with a hairline and space. Rules and rhythm group this page; boxes never do.
Do degrade a wedge label down the ladder (full name → first + initial → truncated first → initials) before dropping it.
Do set anything the surface reports back — the seed, ticket counts — in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do drive the spin through direct style writes on the wheel face, and give reduced-motion users the landed state immediately.
Do keep the wheel, the drawing line, the readout and the spin key inside one viewport by shrinking the wheel, including on a short laptop.
Do keep this route in DARK_EXCEPTIONS — the world is committed light and must never inherit .bx-dark.
donts: Don't give a wedge a colour per name. Three cycling warm neutrals, always.
Don't put the result in a modal or an overlay. The landing happens on the wheel, in place, with the name printed under it.
Don't introduce a card, panel, or raised container. Nothing rests above the ground here except the wheel's own parts and a pressed key.
Don't add a second filled control. One orange key per screen; every other action is quiet or a link.
Don't darken or retint #f26522 to chase a contrast number — a standing PRODUCT.md brand commitment, and it carries no body text on this surface.
Don't add a third ink tone below Dim Ink, or a hairline between every pair of rows and sections at once.
Don't use a pill or a large corner radius. Controls are 3px.
Don't put anything interactive in the bottom-right gutter below 30rem; the site's fixed mobile menu button is parked there.
Don't animate anything for decoration. The spin, the flapper, the landing and the key press are the complete motion vocabulary.
Don't carry .dr-* tokens or classes onto Broadcast Dark, Match Mixer, Pickle Point Pal, Booking Buddy or On Deck, or theirs onto this route.
